History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
41-year-old man with a long-standing history of anxiety presents with a new, severe left-sided headache that woke him at 05:30 today; concern for tension-type versus migraine headache.  

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden onset severe headache, localized to the left side of the head.  
• Onset/Durations: Began early this morning (~05:30); woke patient from sleep; still present at time of call (afternoon).  
• Progression: Constant since onset; no prior episode of this severity or location.  
• Character: Described as “really horrible,” worse initially when lying down but improves slightly once settled.  
• Exacerbating/Relieving factors: Paracetamol taken—no relief. Slightly better after lying down for a while.  
• Associated symptoms: Mild photophobia (“bright lights make eyes a little sore”), transient morning dizziness (resolved). Denies neck stiffness, fever, significant nausea, or vomiting.  
• Similar episodes: History of milder, frontal “cluster” headaches; never unilateral or this severe. No formal migraine diagnosis.  
• Psychosocial stressors: High work stress for ~2 months, frequent late nights.  
• Review of systems (pertinent negatives): No visual disturbance, focal neurological deficit, weakness, speech changes, scalp tenderness, jaw claudication, or recent head trauma.  

Past Medical History:
• Generalized anxiety disorder (diagnosed ≈2 years ago); no complications noted.  
• Denies hypertension or other chronic illnesses.  
• No prior blood pressure evaluations documented.  

Medications:
• Sertraline – dose/route/frequency not documented (ongoing).  
• Paracetamol – self-administered today for headache; dose/route/frequency not documented.  

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.  

Social History:
• Lives with partner; has a cat.  
• Non-smoker.  
• Alcohol/substance use not discussed.  
• Regular exercise: runs ~3×/week.  
• Diet described as “okay,” neither particularly healthy nor unhealthy.  
• Work: Currently stressful with backlog; working late nights.  

Family History:
• Mother with history of anxiety.  
• No family history of migraine or other significant illnesses reported.  

Physical Examination:
(Not performed – telephone consultation)  
• Vitals: not available.  
• General / HEENT / Neuro: no in-person findings.  

Investigations:
• None ordered or available at this visit.  

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute left-sided headache – likely tension-type vs migraine.  
  • Start Ibuprofen (higher migraine-effective dosing; specific dose not documented).  
  • May continue Paracetamol as needed.  
  • Provide written information on red-flag headache symptoms; advise urgent review if these occur.  
  • Encourage hydration (≥1.5-2 L non-caffeinated fluids/day) and adequate sleep (7-8 h/night).  
  • Arrange follow-up in 1 week; earlier review if worsening or new symptoms.  
  • Consider blood tests and further assessment if no improvement at follow-up.  

Issue 2: Work-related stress / underlying anxiety.  
  • Recommend one-week self-certified sick leave to reduce stress.  
  • Provide link for local counseling service – patient to self-refer.  
  • Continue Sertraline; monitor mental health status.  

General plan items:  
  • Reinforce avoidance of medication overuse headache (limit analgesic days).  
  • Maintain regular exercise as tolerated.  

Quality checks:

Missing/expected elements:
• No vitals, neurological or fundoscopic examination documented (telephone consult limitation).  
• Medication doses, routes, and frequencies not specified.  
• Alcohol use and caffeine intake not specifically addressed.  

Internal conflicts:
• None noted within transcript.  

Transcript quality:
• Clear telephone audio; no significant inaudible sections.
